title: Linear threshold functions determined by low-degree coefficients
statement: Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, and let $f,g:\\{-1,1\\}^n\\to\\{-1,1\\}$. Suppose $f$ is a linear threshold function: its value is the sign of an affine linear form in the coordinates, with the convention that a nonnegative input has sign $1$. If the real-valued versions of $f$ and $g$ have equal Fourier coefficients on every set of coordinates of size at most one, then $g=f$.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ is represented as the threshold sign of an affine linear form
